newsitem.title: CHINA: China swing factor in world metals market - analyst.
newsitem.headline: China swing factor in world metals market - analyst.

text.p: While China's net imports and exports of copper, aluminium, nickel, zinc, lead and tin varied in their impact on Western markets, China's unpredictability made it a swing factor in market movements, said a senior metals analyst on Sunday.

"It is not volume that gives China its influence, rather it is that often it acts as a swing factor and also that China's role in international markets is often unpredictable," said Robin Bhar, head of research at Brandeis (Brokers) Limited.
He was addressing a conference on commodity and trade financing organised by Shangxiang Minmetals Holdings Limited in the south China city across the border from Hong Kong.

"For example, in the Western lead market last year, a totally unpredicted 64 percent rise in Chinese refined lead exports to 240,000 tonnes was sufficient to erase a widely forecast deficit and push the market into small surplus," Bhar said.

When equated to total Western demand, the impact of net Chinese exports or imports varied from negligible in the case of nickel, to between one and four percent for copper, aluminium and zinc, to almost five percent for lead and as high as 20 percent for tin, Bhar said.
"Chinese net exports of zinc in 1996 totalled 207,000 tonnes, equal only to 3.3 percent of total western demand," Bhar said.

But based on excess domestic production over domestic consumption of 300,000 tonnes per year, there remained a large risk that China would increase zinc metal exports to the West particularly if prices climbed above US$1,200 per tonne, Bhar said.
